blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Route optimisation in practice is less glamorous than the name suggests. It is dozens of small wins every week: shaving a left turn here, avoiding a traffic pocket there, combining two half-full vans into one. None of them is dramatic alone. All of them together change the economics of an operation.

A good optimisation team starts with data: actual stop times, actual traffic patterns, actual distances — not averages. It then models different route plans against the same day's real demand and picks the one that would have delivered more stops in less time. Over a few months, this iterative discipline usually reduces miles driven by ten to fifteen per cent.

The trick is to avoid the one-time 'big optimisation' that looks great on a slide but never runs a second time. Real gains come from weekly routine, not from quarterly heroics.

items.q: According to the text, what does route optimisation actually consist of?
options: One dramatic redesign of the whole network
Dozens of small wins every week
items.why: "It is dozens of small wins every week" — nenhum sozinho é dramático.

items.q: What does a good optimisation team start with?
options: Actual data: stop times, traffic patterns, distances
items.why: "starts with data: actual stop times, actual traffic patterns, actual distances — not averages."

items.q: Over a few months, how much does the iterative discipline usually reduce miles driven?
options: It does not reduce miles at all
items.why: "usually reduces miles driven by ten to fifteen per cent."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Small weekly adjustments add up to real savings.
A one-time 'big optimisation' on a slide is what really changes the economics.
Optimisation should be a weekly routine.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta contra o 'big optimisation' de uma vez só — o ganho vem da rotina semanal.

items.q: The phrase "never runs a second time" suggests that the big one-off optimisation…
options: is cheaper than the weekly routine
delivers more stops in less time
items.why: Inferência: se não se repete, não gera o ganho contínuo — impressiona no slide mas não muda a operação.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando doze semanas de dados de rota. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks everyone. Before I show you the number, I want to be honest about how we got it, because it isn't a headline project.

Over the last twelve weeks we've made small changes to the routes almost every single day. We removed a few awkward left turns, we rerouted two vans around a traffic pocket near the depot, and on Fridays we combined two half-full runs into one. On its own, none of that is impressive. You wouldn't put any single change on a slide.

But here is what twelve weeks of that discipline adds up to. Miles driven fell by eleven per cent, down to just under nine thousand a week. No new vehicles, no restructure, no big optimisation project — just a habit of looking at the real data every Monday and adjusting.

So my recommendation is simple. Please don't ask me for a one-off, quarterly optimisation. Let me keep the weekly routine instead. The heroics look good in a meeting, but they never run twice. The boring weekly habit is the thing that actually moves the needle.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: By how much did miles driven fall over the twelve weeks?
items.why: "Miles driven fell by eleven per cent, down to just under nine thousand a week."

items.q: Which changes did Harry mention making?
options: Buying new vans and hiring drivers
Removing awkward left turns, rerouting around a traffic pocket, combining half-full runs
items.why: Ele cita as viradas à esquerda, o desvio do engarrafamento e a combinação de duas rotas meio vazias.

items.q: What does Harry ask the team NOT to request?
options: A weekly review of the data
items.why: "Please don't ask me for a one-off, quarterly optimisation. Let me keep the weekly routine instead."

items.q: What does Harry imply about the eleven per cent result?
options: It is the sum of many small, unglamorous adjustments
It came from a single dramatic decision
It was mostly luck, not method
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que nenhuma mudança sozinha impressiona, mas a soma de doze semanas dá o resultado.

items.q: Why does Harry say the 'heroics' never run twice?
options: Because a one-off project impresses in the room but isn't a repeatable habit
Because they are too expensive to repeat
items.why: Inferência: o projeto único fica bonito na reunião, mas não vira rotina — é o hábito semanal que move o ponteiro.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The work is steady, not glamorous — mostly spreadsheets and small tweaks." Glamorous means…
items.why: Glamorous = glamoroso, chamativo/impressionante — o oposto do trabalho discreto do dia a dia.

items.q: "If we shave two minutes off every stop, the whole route finishes earlier." To shave here means to…
items.why: To shave = reduzir (raspar) um pouco de tempo ou distância.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We ___ several route plans against the same day's real demand before choosing one."
items.why: To model = modelar: simular diferentes planos com dados reais.

items.q: "Optimisation is an iterative process." Iterative means…
options: repeated and improved step by step
items.why: Iterative = iterativo: repetido em ciclos, melhorando a cada volta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Real gains come from weekly ___, not from quarterly ___."
items.why: A tese da lição: ganho vem da disciplina semanal, não dos heroísmos trimestrais.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões sobre operações e melhoria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "This weekly habit is what actually moves the needle on cost." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The operations director still has to sign off on the new routing plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new route plan region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two drivers pushed back on the new Friday combined run." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the changes but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry them to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
